title: - Venerable Kotthika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?... Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor does not exist after death?... When asked thus, the venerable…
content: - Venerable Kotthika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?... Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor does not exist after death?... When asked thus, the venerable one answers: 'The Blessed One does not answer: "The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."' For what reason, venerable sir, for what condition does the Blessed One not answer that question?" - "Friend, for one who has lust for form, who delights in form, who rejoices in form, who does not truly know and see the cessation of form, that person may have the view: 'The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' Friend, for one who has lust for feeling... for perception... for formations... Friend, for one who has lust for consciousness, who delights in consciousness, who rejoices in consciousness, who does not truly know and see the cessation of consciousness, that person may have the view: 'The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' Friend, this is the cause, this is the condition, this is the reason why the Blessed One does not answer that question.

title: 'Empty is the world, empty is the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is the world called empty?" - "Because, Ānanda,…
content: 'Empty is the world, empty is the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is the world called empty?" - "Because, Ānanda, the world is empty of self and of anything belonging to self, therefore the world is called empty. And what, Ānanda, is empty of self and of anything belonging to self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Forms are empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Eye-consciousness is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Eye-contact is empty ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact ... that feeling is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. ... The ear ... The nose ... The tongue ... The body ... The mind is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Mind-objects ... Mind-consciousness ... Mind-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact ... that feeling is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. And because it is empty of self and of anything belonging to self, Ānanda, the world is called empty.

title: Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in…
content:
Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in work, is devoted to delight in work; delights in talking, takes pleasure in talking, is devoted to delight in talking; delights in sleeping, takes pleasure in sleeping, is devoted to delight in sleeping.

A bhikkhu who delights in work,
Delights in talking,
Delights in sleeping,
Is restless and agitated.
Such a bhikkhu cannot attain
Supreme enlightenment.

Therefore, let him have few duties,
Little sleep, no restlessness,
Such a bhikkhu can attain
Supreme enlightenment.

title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with such…
content: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with such robes as he receives here and there; is content with such almsfood as he receives here and there; is content with such lodgings as he receives here and there; is content with such medicinal requisites as he receives here and there; and he dwells with many thoughts of renunciation. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha.

title: Here, friends, a person has defilements but does not truly understand: 'There are defilements within me.' For such a person, this can be expected: 'He…
content: Here, friends, a person has defilements but does not truly understand: 'There are defilements within me.' For such a person, this can be expected: 'He will not arouse desire, will not make effort, will not arouse energy to abandon those defilements. He will die while still having greed, still having hatred, still having delusion, still having defilements, still having a defiled mind.' Friends, just as a bronze bowl, brought from the market or from the smithy, covered with dust and grime, and its owner does not use it, does not clean it, and throws it into a dusty place. Friends, after a time, that bowl becomes even more defiled, even dustier.

title: An Arahant bhikkhu, Who has done what had to be done, The taints destroyed, This body, his last body. Can he say: 'I speak'? Can…
content:
An Arahant bhikkhu,
Who has done what had to be done,
The taints destroyed,
This body, his last body.
Can he say:
'I speak'?
Can he say:
'They speak to me'?
( Blessed One ):
An Arahant bhikkhu,
Who has done what had to be done,
The taints destroyed,
This body, his last body.
He can say:
'I speak',
He can say:
'They speak to me'.
Skilfully knowing
Mere conventions in the world,
Using such conventions,
He would speak accordingly.

title: ( Blessed One ): Thinking oneself equal, better, or worse, Conflict arises from that; One who is unmoved by these three, For them equal and…
content:
( Blessed One ):
Thinking oneself equal, better, or worse,
Conflict arises from that;
One who is unmoved by these three,
For them equal and better do not arise.

Give up reckoning,
Do not chase after vain thoughts,
Abandon all craving
For name-and-form in the world.
That one cuts the fetters,
Without worry, without craving.
Devas and humans,
In this world or the next,
In the deva realms,
Or in any abode,
Searching, they cannot find
The footprint of that one.

Throughout the world, do not do
Evil by body, speech, or mind.
Abandon all sensual desires,
Mindful, with clear comprehension,
Without torturing the body,
Vain and unbeneficial.

title: Elder Samiddatta: The five aggregates are fully known, Standing with roots cut off. The end of suffering is attained; I have attained the destruction of…
content:
Elder Samiddatta:

The five aggregates are fully known,
Standing with roots cut off.
The end of suffering is attained; I have attained the destruction of taints.

title: One who dwells in a view, considering it supreme, Placing it highest in the world, Says all others are inferior, Thus he does not transcend…
content:
One who dwells in a view, considering it supreme,
Placing it highest in the world,
Says all others are inferior,
Thus he does not transcend disputes.

When he sees a gain for himself in what is seen, heard,
Virtue, observance, or feeling,
There he grasps, he considers others as inferior.

The skilled say that is a bond — relying on which one regards others as inferior.
Therefore, a bhikkhu should not rely on what is seen, heard, felt, or observance.

Should not construct a view in the world by knowledge or by virtue,
Nor consider oneself equal or inferior;
Not thinking 'superior' or 'inferior'.

Having abandoned the self, not grasping anything,
Not depending on knowledge, not following factions,
Not holding to any view at all.

title: And, bhikkhus, what are the things to be fully understood? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be…
content: And, bhikkhus, what are the things to be fully understood? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be fully understood; perception is a thing to be fully understood; formations are things to be fully understood; consciousness is a thing to be fully understood. These, bhikkhus, are the things to be fully understood. And, bhikkhus, what is full understanding? The destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion, bhikkhus, is called full understanding.
